args.message: Fix money rounding to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP` while FIN-212 requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build's `tests/test_money.py` to fail (e.g. `2.665` was rounding to `2.67` instead of `2.66`).

## Change
- Switched `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch passed (tests/test_money.py green).
args.head: fix/money-bankers-rounding
args.title: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in money rounding (FIN-212)

Done. Here's what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the failure**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but `tests/test_money.py` (per FIN-212) expects banker's rounding — e.g. `2.665` should round to `2.66`, not `2.67`.
2. **Created branch** `fix/money-bankers-rounding` off main.
3. **Fixed the code**: changed the rounding mode in `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (the docstring already said it should be banker's rounding per FIN-212).
4. **Ran CI**: run `ci-0001` on the branch **passed**.
5. **Opened PR #102** against `main` with alex requested as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/102

The PR is now awaiting code-owner review before it can be merged into main (main is protected, so I did not merge it).

transcript.reasoning_content: Let me look at the repo files first.

Note: test expects 2.675 -> 2.68 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN. In Decimal, 2.675 quantize half-even: 2.675 -> last digit 7, rounding half-even: 2.675 is exactly halfway between 2.67 and 2.68; half-even rounds to even last digit: 2.68 (8 even). Yes. 2.665 -> halfway between 2.66 and 2.67; half-even rounds to 2.66 (6 even). Good.

Create branch, commit fix.
